title: Ludic Involvement
role_in_volume: DIMENSION CHAPTER 6 (of 6). The structurally most elaborated dimension chapter in the volume — eight named subsections, including a closing 'Ludic Involvement Summary' that is unique among the six dimension chapters and signals the structural end of the dimension-chapter cycle (Ch.10 immediately commences the synthesis). Operationalizes the LUDIC dimension as engagement with the rule system through goal-pursuit, plan-formulation, decision-making, and the receipt of rewards. Introduces Calleja's primary analytic innovation in the volume's dimension chapters — the STRATEGY / TACTICS / MICROTACTICS three-tier planning hierarchy — and supplies an implicit eight-category rewards typology. The chapter is also the volume's PREMIER anticipatory-bridge site for Aristotelian phronesis + deliberative phantasia, Burke's Purpose+Act ratio, and Uexküll's Wirkmal/Funktionskreis vocabulary.

outline.title: Macro Phase: Goals and Rewards (Caillois paidia/ludus + rule-systems + ergodic-semiosis + macro/micro orientation)
outline.summary: Opens with Caillois's paidia/ludus distinction (block-quoted three times, pp.147-148): paidia as 'diversion, turbulence, free improvisation, and carefree gaiety' / 'uncontrolled fantasy,' an idealized pre-linguistic purity of play; ludus as 'gratuitous' structure that disciplines and enriches paidia, providing occasion for training, skill-acquisition, and conventional problem-solving. Calleja immediately qualifies: digital games can never attain Caillois's paidic ideal because they are coded — even free-form Liberty City flight in GTA IV is shaped by the rule system; the player's intention is 'always limited by the conventions of a designed system' (p.148). Pivot to the rules-give-meaning argument via Salen+Zimmerman (2003) + Juul (2005) + Malaby (2007): the rule system is 'the machine behind the representational surface' (p.148) generating a 'landscape of interesting choices' and 'interesting forms of contingency.' Ergodic-vs-non-ergodic semiosis is illustrated via the Call of Duty IV capture-the-flag paradigm (pp.148-149): a national flag in a film carries patriotic connotations, but in capture-the-flag the flag becomes 'the locus of a competitive struggle' whose meanings can be understood only through rule-mediated interaction. Closing: rules rarely focus conscious attention; the rule system manifests itself experientially via goal-pursuit and decision-making (p.149). The macro/micro orientation paragraph defines macro-phase ludic involvement as motivation-via-goal-and-reward and micro-phase as moment-to-moment decision-making and plan-formulation within a hierarchy of self-set, system-set, or community-set goals.

outline.title: Goals (autotelic loanword + Schank+Abelson instrumental goals + system/self/community taxonomy + GTA IV + Oblivion + WoW Ananke + Sunniva agency interlude)
outline.summary: Choices in games gravitate to goal-pursuit, either system-set or player-set. Calleja flags that goal-pursuit can be 'an end in itself — an autotelic experience yielding satisfaction within a rule-based system of meaning — or it can be fueled by the desire of attaining a reward' (p.149) — deploying the autotelic loanword without citing Csikszentmihalyi (Layer-A anchor site for Aristotelian eudaimonia / praxis-for-its-own-sake). Game-goals are designed to be attainable in a way life-goals are not (Egenfeldt-Nielsen+Smith+Tosca 2008; Juul 2005). Järvinen's doctoral block-quote (p.150): games 'distil the abstract life goals … into highly concrete, temporally and spatially circumscribed events.' Multiple theorists (Juul, Salen+Zimmerman, Järvinen, Björk+Holopainen) converge that goals are central. Three-source taxonomy: goals can be system-determined, individually-determined, or community-negotiated. GTA IV (pp.150-151) coordinates strict-mission goals with personal goals (drive-around-for-a-nicer-car, with Schank+Abelson 'instrumental goal' framing) and community-negotiated mini-games (player-arranged hospital-loop races). Space Invaders (p.151) bounds personal-goal scope to the narrow activity-range of the game system; Oblivion + Fallout 3 (pp.151-152) supply the sandbox alternative-primary-goal paradigm (choose criminal-career-by-rule-system-validation rather than save-the-world). MMOG scope is broadest but still rule-constrained (first-level WoW character cannot freely explore). Ananke's Darkshore swim (p.152) is the chapter's signature self-set-goal exhibit; the swim doesn't yield system rewards but explores 'the limits of traversing game space.' The cross-dimensional weaving paragraph (p.153) explicitly thematizes that ludic involvement co-operates with spatial + kinesthetic involvement (this is the chapter's sole occurrence of 'agency' — 'the sense of agency created by allowing players to decide to do something and then to actually do it'). Sunniva's Planetside quote (p.153) anchors the player-control argument: more self-set-goal scope makes the game 'more engaging … 'cause you need to plan more and think more around what you're doing.'

outline.title: The Structure of Goals (cognitive-psychology hierarchy bundle + Järvinen primary-vs-sub + Björk+Holopainen pattern + Fallout 3 cascade + Far Cry 2 respawn + McIntosh partial-rejection + numbers-game Oriel)
outline.summary: Cognitive-psychology consensus (Bell+Huang 1997; Locke+Latham 1990; McIntosh 1996; Rosenbloom+Newell 1983): goals are hierarchically structured into primary-goals and subgoals; immediately-attainable subgoals are pursued instrumentally toward primary goals (Houser-Marko 2007). Järvinen (2008) applies the distinction to games; Björk+Holopainen (2005) identify the hierarchy as a recurring design pattern and observe that player-awareness of the lower-to-higher-order linkage raises satisfaction. Fallout 3 cascade example (pp.153-154): primary goal find-fugitive-father → subgoal travel-to-radio-station → subgoal procure-equipment → subgoal find-town (Megaton) → subgoal earn-bottle-cap-currency → subgoal find-a-job. The primary goal is essential because it gives meaning to the consequent subgoal chain and motivates continued engagement. Rule-system support determines whether alternative-personal-primary-goals are sustainable: Fallout 3 supports a murder-everyone-in-the-world primary goal because corpses persist; Far Cry 2 (p.154) does not, because enemies respawn infinitely. The 'lack of a clearly defined primary goal' / 'requirement of adhering to a system-determined primary goal' tension is calibrated to game-genre expectations (tennis games do not need open worlds; MMOGs do). Game-life-goal relativity (p.154): the entire game-activity can itself be a subgoal of out-of-game primary-goals (relaxation, self-worth-via-competition). McIntosh's claim that hierarchically-higher goals are more abstract is PARTIALLY REJECTED for games (p.155): primary game-goals are typically concrete and explicitly communicated (highest-MMOG-level displayed at all times) because games are designed for sustained engagement. Oriel's WoW quote on the numbers-game (p.155) closes the subsection.

outline.title: Micro Phase: Plans, Goals, and Rewards during Gameplay (Sid Meier 'set of interesting choices' axiom via Rollings+Morris + ergodicity recall)
outline.summary: Brief pivot section. Sid Meier (quoted in Rollings+Morris 2000, p.38): games are 'a set of interesting choices'; players' ability to formulate and execute plans is constitutive. Micro-phase ludic involvement concerns engagement with the decision-making process and the perceived consequences of action. Calleja recalls Ch.3's definition of ergodicity as comprising cognitive activity in plan-formulation, readiness-to-act, and execution-of-act. Note: the Sid Meier aphorism functions as the chapter's working analog for Salen+Zimmerman's 'meaningful choice,' but Calleja does not use the Salen+Zimmerman term — and Sid Meier reaches Calleja only via Rollings+Morris (a game-design-practice book), not from primary Meier writing.

outline.title: Plans and Goals (iterative planning/execution/feedback/replanning loop + WoW Ratchet-Feathermoon + multiplayer micro-planning + Spore dual-goal)
outline.summary: Action-execution is the actualization of a plan to attain a goal. The engaging structure of digital games is the iterative loop: players formulate subgoal plans, execute, receive feedback on success-likelihood, then continue or modify the plan; failed plans yield restart-and-try-again; successful subgoals advance the chain. Ludic micro-phase involvement is the initiation of plan-actualization through exploration of available options and consequence-perception across systemic, personal, and social goal-types. WoW Ratchet-to-Feathermoon journey (p.156) is the in-vivo exemplar: plans amended on the spot when unforeseen skirmishes erupt. Multiplayer + open-MMOG situational complexity exceeds the scope of game rules. Other micro-phase planning instances: WoW auction-house pricing, Counter-Strike: Source defensive strategy, Medieval II: Total War siege-of-Aragon. Spore creature-customization (p.156): a personal-goal (fit a specific mental image) and a systemic-goal (build a functionally aggressive creature) can co-exist within the same activity; the activity is ludic-involvement iff goal-geared, not iff agonistic.

outline.title: Strategies, Tactics, and Microtactics (Calleja's analytic innovation — three-tier planning hierarchy + fencing extended example + temporal-distance qualification + FIFA 09 Ultimate Team extended case + right-winger microtactic)
outline.summary: CALLEJA'S PRIMARY ANALYTIC INNOVATION IN THIS CHAPTER. The primary-goal/subgoal distinction entails a parallel plan-level distinction: plans-in-pursuit-of-primary-goals are STRATEGIES; plans-in-pursuit-of-subgoals are TACTICS; plans-formulated-during-the-moment-of-action are MICROTACTICS. The three-tier typology is presented as a heuristic gradient, not rigid labeling. Fencing extended example (pp.157-158): primary goal = be ranked top-three in county; tactical level = win-individual-matches at an upcoming tournament; microtactic level = within-a-match, on-the-spot decisions to attain the immediate goal of winning the current point. Calleja supplies a microtactic example formulated as inner-speech: 'He is out of balance, with the foil moving clockwise; lunge with a counterclockwise evasion of the blade' (p.158). TEMPORAL-DISTANCE QUALIFICATION: the strategy/tactic/microtactic distinction is useful only where there is a short temporal distance between plan-formulation, execution, feedback, and evaluation; turn-based board games do not benefit from microtactic vocabulary because players have time to think tactically. The microtactic concept identifies 'decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others.' FIFA 09 Ultimate Team extended case (pp.158-159): personal primary goal = build an all-Italian team and win an online cup; subgoal cascade = earn match-money / preserve contract-time / hire staff (manager, head-coach, goalkeeper-trainer, physiotherapist, fitness-instructor) / develop chosen players / preserve player morale (contradictory because morale requires playing-time but contract-time is finite). The interlocking ludic-economy of contract-time + money + staff + morale is the chapter's most elaborated single design-economy analysis (capture as ludic-economy reasoning even though Calleja does not use the phrase). Microtactic exemplar: right-winger faced by a defender — short-pass-to-right-back, dribble-and-cross, or cross-immediately — is an individual microtactic in service of higher-order tactics.

outline.title: Rewards (subjective-value framing + Planetside skill-point ability-economy + Oblivion/LOTRO mobility-reward + RTS fog-of-war visibility-reward + GTA IV spatial-reward + Counter-Strike 'Monster Kill' + achievements + numbers-game + WoW Aprile grinding + competitive rewards + collaborative rewards/Priest healing + scripted-narrative rewards/Nico + MGS4 anti-paradigm + aesthetic-beauty rewards + Flower paradigm)
outline.summary: Longest subsection. Rewards are delivered incrementally as the player advances through designed structures-of-progression. Reward-value is essentially subjective: the same cut-scene delights one player and annoys another; a rare magic-hammer is precious to one player and trivial to another. Implicit eight-category rewards typology: (1) PERFORMATIVE-ENHANCING rewards — improve avatar/miniature abilities, with Planetside skill-point ability-economy as paradigm (p.159): skill-points buy access to armor, weapons, vehicles; new skills compound with prior skills (infiltrator-suit + reconnaissance-aircraft synergy). (2) MOBILITY-ENHANCING rewards — efficient/attractive navigation of large worlds; Oblivion's Cyrodill and LOTRO's Middle-earth (p.160) as exemplars; mount/horse/pony purchase in MMOGs. (3) VISIBILITY/SPATIAL rewards — fog-of-war RTS map-revealing abilities (p.160). (4) SPATIAL-AREA-AS-REWARD — GTA IV's mission-gated area unlocks (p.160). (5) INTRINSIC-VALUE rewards — points/score in arcade games (Space Invaders), with Counter-Strike: Source's exaggerated 'Monster Kill' sound effect as the rhetorical-amplification paradigm (p.161). (6) SOCIAL-ACCLAMATION rewards — achievements systems on contemporary consoles (p.161); bragging-rights in gaming community. (7) THE NUMBERS-GAME — scores increasing, level-meters filling; participants describe continuing-past-intent to reach a new level, log-off-with-closure. Grinding (p.162): repeatedly killing unchallenging creatures purely for XP-efficiency; Aprile (WoW) quote on grinding-as-tedious-but-necessary. Numbers-game applies beyond MMOGs to football-team / city / army quantification. Competitive rewards (p.163): most-kills in Counter-Strike; first-guild-to-defeat-a-raid-boss in WoW. Collaborative rewards: LOTRO Burglar concealment; WoW Priest healing-class — class-choice is a goal/reward orientation choice. (8) SCRIPTED-NARRATIVE rewards: GTA IV's Nico-story cut scenes work because graphics + voice-acting + character-depth; MGS4 (p.164) is the anti-paradigm of overlong cut scenes. AESTHETIC-BEAUTY rewards: GTA IV harbor at sunrise; Flower (p.165) makes aesthetic-beauty an explicit reward — surroundings burst into color upon sequence completion (Figure 9.3 anchor). Affective response: success/failure of goal-attainment is an emotionally charged experience because outcomes reflect dexterous/cognitive/social abilities; the dimension is dominantly stimulation-directed today, though aesthetic-beauty rewards reside on the calmer side of the affective dimension.

outline.title: Ludic Involvement Summary (recap of choices + repercussions + bridge to Ch.10)
outline.summary: Unique-among-dimension-chapters summary subsection. Ludic involvement is 'one of the most fundamental cornerstones of a game' — compelling because of the cognitive challenges + associated rewards games are apt at presenting. Ludic involvement is engagement with choices made in the game and their repercussions; choices may track system-stipulated, player-set, or community-set goals, or may be spur-of-the-moment with no overarching goal-link. WITHOUT REPERCUSSIONS, ACTIONS LOSE MEANING and their execution generates no excitement (the closing one-line statement of the rules-as-meaning-enabler thesis). Final paragraph signposts Ch.10: 'now that we have considered each dimension of the player involvement model in turn, we move on to consider how the model addresses the four challenges discussed in chapter 2,' leading toward the incorporation solution to the presence/immersion question.

dimension_operational_definition: LUDIC INVOLVEMENT is engagement with the rule system through the pursuit of goals (system-set, self-set, or community-negotiated) and the formulation, execution, evaluation, and revision of plans toward those goals — together with the receipt of associated rewards. Macro-phase: motivation by goal-and-reward structures off-line. Micro-phase: moment-to-moment decision-making and plan-formulation in a landscape of interesting choices.

boundary_criteria.criterion: Rule-system mediation present (action-meanings depend on rules)
Goal-orientation (activity is geared toward a specific goal — agonism not required)
Plan-formulation iterative loop (planning / execution / feedback / replanning)

concepts.label: ludic involvement (canonical)
concepts.gloss: Engagement with the rule system through goal-pursuit and decision-making; macro = motivation by goals+rewards, micro = moment-to-moment plan-formulation in a hierarchy of goals.

concepts.label: rules / rule system as machine behind representational surface
concepts.gloss: Rules assign values to objects, events, entities; generate a 'landscape of interesting choices' (Salen+Zimmerman 2003; Juul 2005; Malaby 2007 contingency-via-rules).

concepts.label: paidia (Caillois)
concepts.gloss: Diversion, turbulence, free improvisation, carefree gaiety; idealized pre-linguistic purity of play that no digital game can fully attain due to coded design.

concepts.label: ludus (Caillois)
concepts.gloss: Gratuitous structure imposed upon paidia; disciplines and enriches paidia, providing occasion for skill-acquisition and conventional problem-solving.

concepts.label: ergodic-vs-non-ergodic semiosis (rule-system-frames-representational-layer)
concepts.gloss: Sign-significance in ergodic media is rule-system mediated; Call of Duty IV capture-the-flag flag-as-ludic-objective is the paradigm exhibit (volume-defining Wirkmal candidate).

concepts.label: rule-system manifests itself experientially through goal-pursuit
concepts.gloss: Rules rarely focus conscious attention; the system manifests experientially as decision-making and the pursuit of personal and game-defined goals.

concepts.label: goal-source taxonomy (system / self / community)
concepts.gloss: Three-way taxonomy: game-system-determined goals, individually-player-determined goals, community-negotiated goals (multiplayer).

concepts.label: personal-goal-scope as function of game-system activity-range
concepts.gloss: Space Invaders constrains personal-goal scope severely; Oblivion / Fallout 3 sandbox widens it; MMOG widens further. Personal-goal possibility depends on rule-system affordances.

concepts.label: instrumental goal (Schank+Abelson 1977)
concepts.gloss: A goal that acts as a prerequisite to another goal; Calleja's bridge from cognitive-AI script-theory into game-goal hierarchy.

concepts.label: goal-hierarchy primary/sub structure
concepts.gloss: Cognitive-psychology consensus (Bell+Huang, Locke+Latham, McIntosh, Rosenbloom+Newell, Houser-Marko); applied to games by Järvinen 2008 and Björk+Holopainen 2005. Subgoals pursued instrumentally toward primary goals.

concepts.label: primary-goal concreteness in games (McIntosh partial-rejection)
concepts.gloss: McIntosh's hierarchically-higher-=-more-abstract claim is rejected for games: primary game-goals are typically concrete and explicitly communicated for sustained-engagement design.

concepts.label: alternative-personal-primary-goal (rule-system support)
concepts.gloss: Fallout 3 supports a murder-everyone-in-the-world primary goal because corpses persist; Far Cry 2 cannot, because enemies respawn infinitely. Rule-system support is the determining condition.

concepts.label: game-as-subgoal-of-life-goal relativity
concepts.gloss: The entire game-activity can itself be a subgoal of out-of-game primary-goals (relaxation, self-worth-via-competition).

concepts.label: 'set of interesting choices' (Sid Meier via Rollings+Morris)
concepts.gloss: Working axiom for micro-phase ludic involvement. Source: quoted in Rollings+Morris 2000, p.38 (not from a Meier primary source). Functions as Calleja's working analog for Salen+Zimmerman 'meaningful choice' (which he does not use).

concepts.label: iterative planning loop (plan / execute / feedback / replan)
concepts.gloss: Micro-phase signature: subgoal plan formulated, plan executed, feedback received on likelihood-of-success, plan continued or modified or restarted; on subgoal-completion, new subgoal engaged (often higher in hierarchy).

concepts.label: strategies (plans in pursuit of primary goals)
concepts.gloss: First tier of Calleja's three-tier planning hierarchy. Plans-in-pursuit-of-primary-goals.

concepts.label: tactics (plans in pursuit of subgoals)
concepts.gloss: Second tier. Plans-in-pursuit-of-subgoals.

concepts.label: microtactics (plans during moment of action)
concepts.gloss: Calleja's introduced term — plans formulated during the moment of action under conditions of short temporal-distance between formulation, execution, feedback, and evaluation. Identifies 'decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others.'

concepts.label: strategy/tactics/microtactics three-tier hierarchy (Calleja's analytic innovation)
concepts.gloss: The chapter's primary distinctive theoretical contribution. Heuristic gradient (not rigid labeling) mapping plan-level to goal-level via temporal-granularity of planning-execution-feedback cycle. PRIMARY DISSERTATION-INSTRUMENT CANDIDATE.

concepts.label: temporal-distance qualification on microtactic
concepts.gloss: The microtactic concept is useful only where plan-formulation, execution, feedback, and evaluation are close in time; turn-based board-games do not benefit from microtactic vocabulary.

concepts.label: ludic economy (anticipatory term-of-art; FIFA 09 contract-time/money/staff/morale interlock)
concepts.gloss: Extended FIFA 09 Ultimate Team case: contract-time + money + staff-hire + player-morale form an interlocking economy of scarce resources allocated under primary-goal constraint. Calleja does not use 'ludic economy' as a term — anticipatory naming.

concepts.label: rewards typology (eight implicit categories)
concepts.gloss: Performative-enhancing / mobility-enhancing / visibility-spatial / spatial-area-unlock / intrinsic-points / social-acclamation-achievements / numbers-game / scripted-narrative / aesthetic-beauty. Anticipatory formalization of Calleja's implicit eight-fold categorization.

concepts.label: subjective-value framing of reward
concepts.gloss: Reward-value depends on player's wants, needs, expectations; same cut-scene delights one and annoys another.

concepts.label: autotelic (loanword without Csikszentmihalyi)
concepts.gloss: Calleja: goal-pursuit can be 'an end in itself — an autotelic experience yielding satisfaction within a rule-based system of meaning.' Csikszentmihalyi not cited — confirms volume-wide flow-theory absence. Layer-A anchor site for Aristotelian eudaimonia / praxis-for-its-own-sake.

concepts.label: agency (single occurrence — sense of agency via decide-and-do)
concepts.gloss: Calleja's sole use of 'agency' in Ch.9: 'the sense of agency created by allowing players to decide to do something and then to actually do it.' Agency-theorization proper sits in Ch.4 Kinesthetic; here it operates as a felt-experiential residue (RESIDUAL-PHENOMENOLOGY-WITHOUT-PHENOMENOLOGIST-CITE flag).

concepts.label: contingency (Malaby 2007)
concepts.gloss: Rule systems intended to generate 'interesting forms of contingency' for players to test and explore. Single-cite functional anchor.

concepts.label: the numbers game (player participant idiom)
concepts.gloss: Player orientation toward maximizing quantifiable progress — level, XP, gold, gear-stats. Oriel + Aprile WoW quotes anchor.

concepts.label: grinding
concepts.gloss: Repetitive killing of unchallenging creatures purely for XP efficiency; admittedly tedious, lure-of-next-level makes it worthwhile (Aprile quote).

concepts.label: achievement-as-bragging-rights (social-acclamation reward)
concepts.gloss: Predefined-goal-unlock displayed on player profile; satisfaction of completion takes the form of bragging-rights in gaming community.

concepts.label: collaborative rewards (class-choice as orientation)
concepts.gloss: LOTRO Burglar concealment + WoW Priest healing-class: class-selection commits player to a particular reward-orientation toward assisting others.

concepts.label: scripted-narrative-as-reward / overlong-cut-scene anti-paradigm
concepts.gloss: GTA IV Nico-story works (graphics + voice + character-depth); MGS4 hour-long cut scenes fail because non-skippable + tedious. Reward only when the player cannot bypass it AND finds it captivating.

concepts.label: aesthetic-beauty-as-reward (Flower paradigm)
concepts.gloss: Aesthetic appreciation on calmer side of affective dimension. GTA IV harbor at sunrise; Flower's explicit reward-mechanic: sequence-completion bursts surroundings into color (Figure 9.3 anchor).

concepts.label: cross-dimensional weaving (ludic ↔ spatial ↔ kinesthetic)
concepts.gloss: Ananke's Darkshore swim makes explicit that ludic involvement does not operate in isolation — goal-completion is supported by sense-of-agency (kinesthetic-adjacent) and exploration of game-space (spatial).

concepts.label: Caillois paidia-shaped-by-code (paidia-impossibility for digital games)
concepts.gloss: Even the most free-form digital activity is shaped by coded rules. GTA IV Liberty City reckless flying as exhibit.

concepts.label: research-participant testimony as evidence-mode
concepts.anchor: Ananke p.152; Sunniva p.153; Oriel p.155; Aprile p.162
concepts.gloss: Four participant voices — three WoW (Ananke, Oriel, Aprile) + one Planetside (Sunniva) — anchor key arguments about self-set goals, the numbers-game, and grinding.

concepts.label: without-repercussions-actions-lose-meaning (summary closing thesis)
concepts.gloss: Chapter-closing one-line restatement of the rules-as-meaning-enabler thesis. Tightest summary of the agency-vs-rules tension's implicit resolution: rule-mediated repercussions are constitutive of meaningful action.

positions.label: Rules CONSTRAIN action but also ENABLE meaning — restriction is constitutive of meaningfulness, not opposed to it
positions.summary: The chapter's implicit resolution of the agency-vs-rules tension. 'The intention of the player is always limited by the conventions of a designed system' AND 'Rules give meaning to actions and objects in the game world' — same paragraph. Closing summary: 'Without repercussions, actions lose their meaning.' Calleja's working position is that rule-constrained choice is the only kind of meaningful choice; this is his closest approach to a Salen+Zimmerman 'meaningful choice' argument without using the term.

positions.label: Goals are central to games; goal-hierarchy structure is recurring; goal-source is a three-way taxonomy (system / self / community)
positions.summary: Synthesizing Caillois + Salen+Zimmerman + Juul + Järvinen + Björk+Holopainen + cognitive-psychology bundle: goals are the experiential interface to the rule system; they are hierarchically structured; they originate from one of three sources, with personal-goal scope conditional on rule-system affordances.

positions.label: Plan-level decomposes into strategy / tactics / microtactics — a three-tier hierarchy tracking goal-tier and temporal-distance of feedback (Calleja's analytic innovation)
positions.summary: Calleja's own term-of-art elaboration. Plans-in-pursuit-of-primary-goals = strategies; plans-in-pursuit-of-subgoals = tactics; plans-formulated-during-moment-of-action under short-temporal-distance feedback = microtactics. The most distinctively Calleja-conceptual move in the chapter.

positions.label: Reward-value is essentially subjective and culturally / dispositionally variable; reward-categories span a typology that is broader than designer-validated point-rewards
positions.summary: Rewards include performative / mobility / visibility / spatial-area / intrinsic-points / social-acclamation / scripted-narrative / aesthetic-beauty. The Counter-Strike 'Monster Kill' audio-amplification and Flower's color-burst aesthetic-reward bracket the typology on the rhetorical-amplification and aesthetic-appreciation poles.

positions.label: Ludic involvement does not operate in isolation — it weaves with kinesthetic + spatial + (in MMOGs) shared involvement
positions.summary: The Ananke-Darkshore-swim paragraph explicitly thematizes cross-dimensional weaving; ludic-agency is supported by spatial-exploration + kinesthetic decide-and-do.

tensions.label: Rules-as-constraint vs. rules-as-meaningful-context
tensions.summary: Same chapter, same paragraph: 'the intention of the player is always limited by the conventions of a designed system' AND 'Rules give meaning to actions and objects in the game world.' Tension is real but Calleja's implicit resolution is that the two clauses are the same thesis read from opposite sides — restriction is constitutive of meaning. The closing summary line 'Without repercussions, actions lose their meaning' is the tightest one-line resolution. Implicit Salen+Zimmerman 'meaningful choice' is reconstructable from this position.

tensions.label: Ludic-agency-as-felt vs. narrative-determination / system-determination
tensions.anchor: p.153 line 5397 (sole agency-occurrence) + pp.154-155 alternative-primary-goal discussion
tensions.summary: The chapter uses 'agency' only once (p.153) and treats it as the felt-experiential residue of decide-and-do under rule-system permission. Yet pp.154-155 show that alternative-personal-primary-goals are conditional on rule-system support: Fallout 3 allows murder-everyone, Far Cry 2 does not. Felt-agency is structurally pre-empted by the designer's choice of respawn-rule. Calleja stops short of Sicart-style ethical-rule-design analysis. RESIDUAL-PHENOMENOLOGY-WITHOUT-PHENOMENOLOGIST-CITE flag applies (no Husserl/Merleau-Ponty/Heidegger anchor for 'sense of agency').

tensions.label: Caillois paidic-ideal vs. coded-game inescapability
tensions.summary: Caillois's paidia is the idealized pre-linguistic purity of play; Calleja immediately concedes that digital games can never attain this ideal because they are coded. The chapter is structurally framed by a tension between the classical aspirational frame (paidia/ludus) and the contemporary digital reality (rule-system everywhere). The tension is not resolved — it is a structural backdrop.

game_loci.title: Grand Theft Auto IV
game_loci.occurrences: RECURRING (paidia-shaped-by-code p.148; system-set+player-set goals coexistence pp.150-151; spatial-area-unlock reward p.160; scripted-narrative Nico-story reward p.164; aesthetic-beauty harbor-at-sunrise reward p.165)
game_loci.analytic_move: The volume's premier ludic-dimension case study — paradigm for every major subsection. Open virtual environment with embedded mini-games + linear scripted-narrative + sandbox personal-goal-setting (drive-around-for-a-nicer-car; player-arranged hospital-loop races); and four distinct reward-modes across the rewards typology.

game_loci.title: Call of Duty IV
game_loci.analytic_move: Capture-the-flag flag-as-ludic-objective paradigm. A national flag in a film carries patriotic connotations; in capture-the-flag the flag becomes the locus of a competitive struggle whose meanings are accessible only through rule-mediated interaction. THE VOLUME-DEFINING EXHIBIT for ergodic-vs-non-ergodic semiosis and the strongest Uexküll Wirkmal (effect-marker) candidate site.

game_loci.title: Space Invaders
game_loci.analytic_move: Minimal personal-goal scope (constrained by narrow rule-system activity-range — clear five levels without dying); arcade-points intrinsic-reward exemplar — points as ludic-intrinsic value.

game_loci.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
game_loci.analytic_move: Sandbox alternative-primary-goal paradigm — choose criminal-career rather than save-the-world; rule-system reacts (notoriety grows, authorities pursue); Cyrodill large-world mobility-reward (horse purchase) exemplar.

game_loci.title: Fallout 3
game_loci.analytic_move: Primary-goal-with-cascading-subgoals paradigm: find fugitive father → radio station → equipment → town (Megaton) → bottle-cap currency → job. Also alternative-primary-goal exhibit: murder-everyone supported because corpses persist.

game_loci.title: Far Cry 2
game_loci.analytic_move: Anti-paradigm to alternative-primary-goal: infinite respawn prevents murder-everyone primary goal. Rule-system design determines which personal-primary-goals are attainable.

game_loci.title: World of Warcraft
game_loci.occurrences: RECURRING (first-level region-restriction p.152; Ananke Darkshore swim p.152; auction-house pricing p.156; raid first-guild reward p.163; Priest healing-class p.164; Aprile grinding p.162; Oriel numbers-game p.155)
game_loci.analytic_move: Second-most-cited game after GTA IV. MMOG-scope personal-goal exemplar; signature self-set-goal (Ananke swim); paradigm for collaborative class-based rewards; primary site for participant-testimony evidence-mode.

game_loci.title: Spore
game_loci.analytic_move: Personal-vs-systemic dual-goal coexistence within single activity: fit-mental-image (personal) + build-functionally-aggressive-creature (systemic). Goal-geared activity need not be agonistic to qualify as ludic involvement.

game_loci.title: Counter-Strike: Source
game_loci.analytic_move: Defensive-strategy micro-phase planning exemplar (p.156); 'Monster Kill' exaggerated-sound-effect rhetorical-amplification of intrinsic-points reward (p.161); most-kills competitive reward (p.163).

game_loci.title: Medieval II: Total War
game_loci.analytic_move: Turn-strategy planning paradigm (siege-of-Aragon army-allocation decision). Anti-microtactic case — turn-based pacing means microtactic vocabulary does not apply.

game_loci.title: FIFA 09
game_loci.analytic_move: Strategy/tactics/microtactics extended case via Ultimate Team mode. Interlocking ludic-economy: contract-time + money + staff (manager/head-coach/goalkeeper-trainer/physiotherapist/fitness-instructor) + player-morale. Right-winger pass/dribble/cross decision is the canonical microtactic example.

game_loci.title: Planetside
game_loci.analytic_move: Skill-point ability-economy paradigm: each skill-point buys access to armor/weapons/vehicles; skill-compounding synergy (infiltrator-suit + reconnaissance-aircraft). Performative-enhancing reward exemplar.

game_loci.title: Lord of the Rings Online
game_loci.analytic_move: Middle-earth scale + horse/pony mobility-reward (p.160); Burglar-class concealment as collaborative reward (p.164). Cross-anchor for mobility-reward + collaborative-reward typology rows.

game_loci.title: Aion: The Tower of Eternity
game_loci.analytic_move: Level-up moment visual anchor for the numbers-game subsection. Image-based exhibit.

game_loci.title: Metal Gear Solid 4
game_loci.analytic_move: Overlong-cut-scene anti-paradigm. Non-skippable hour-long sequences exemplify scripted-narrative-as-reward failure when player cannot bypass and finds it tedious.

game_loci.title: Flower
game_loci.analytic_move: Aesthetic-beauty-as-explicit-reward paradigm. Sequence-completion bursts surroundings into color. Anchors the aesthetic-beauty-as-reward category on the calmer side of the affective dimension.

game_loci.title: Cyrodill (Oblivion game-world)
game_loci.analytic_move: Large-game-world traversal-time exemplar (hours from point-to-point), motivating mobility-reward category.

game_loci.title: Ratchet-to-Feathermoon journey (WoW)
game_loci.analytic_move: Micro-phase plan-formulation exemplar with on-the-spot replanning when unforeseen skirmishes erupt en route.

interlocutors.name: Roger Caillois
interlocutors.role: PRIMARY macro-phase opening anchor — paidia/ludus distinction structures pp.147-148. Block-quoted three times. Classical play-theory frame for the chapter.

interlocutors.name: Katie Salen and Eric Zimmerman
interlocutors.role: Cited p.148 (systemic nature of games / rules-give-meaning) and p.149 (goals-centrality consensus). The 'meaningful choice' construct is the conceptual ancestor of Calleja's rule-system-makes-choice-meaningful argument; Calleja does NOT use the exact phrase 'meaningful choice.'

interlocutors.name: Jesper Juul
interlocutors.role: Cited p.148 (systemic nature of games), p.149 (Egenfeldt-Nielsen+Smith+Tosca+Juul on skill-modulation), p.150 (goals-centrality consensus). Magic-circle critique NOT engaged here — sits in IG-03.

interlocutors.name: Thomas Malaby
interlocutors.work: Beyond Play: A New Approach to Games (2007)
interlocutors.role: Cited p.148 — rules 'intended to generate interesting forms of contingency for the players to test and explore.' Single-cite functional anchor for the contingency-via-rules argument.

interlocutors.name: Roger Schank and Robert Abelson
interlocutors.role: Cited p.151 — supplies 'instrumental goal' construct (a goal that acts as a prerequisite to another goal). Cognitive-AI / script-theory anchor for goal-hierarchy machinery.

interlocutors.name: Aki Järvinen
interlocutors.role: PRIMARY game-theoretic anchor. Block-quoted p.150 ('games … distil the abstract life goals that we struggle with on a daily basis into highly concrete, temporally and spatially circumscribed events'). Applies primary-goal/subgoal distinction to games (p.153). The chapter's heaviest single theoretical interlocutor.

interlocutors.name: Staffan Björk and Jussi Holopainen
interlocutors.role: Cited p.150 (goals-centrality consensus) and p.153 (hierarchy of goals as recurring design pattern; player-awareness of lower-to-higher-order linkage raises satisfaction). Design-pattern anchor.

interlocutors.name: Bell and Huang
interlocutors.role: Cognitive-psychology hierarchical goal-structure consensus bundle (p.153). Bundled citation, not individually engaged.

interlocutors.name: Locke and Latham
interlocutors.work: A Theory of Goal Setting and Task Performance (1990)

interlocutors.name: William McIntosh
interlocutors.role: Cognitive-psychology bundle (p.153); also individually engaged at p.155 — Calleja partially rejects McIntosh's higher-=-more-abstract claim for games.

interlocutors.name: Lisa Houser-Marko
interlocutors.role: Cited p.153 — immediately-attainable subgoals tend to be pursued in order to accomplish primary goals. Single-cite subgoal-pursuit psychology anchor.

interlocutors.name: Simon Egenfeldt-Nielsen, Jonas Heide Smith, and Susana Pajares Tosca
interlocutors.role: Cited p.149 (with Juul) — games 'constitute systems that can be interpreted and modulated to suit the skills of the participants.' Skill-modulation anchor for games-as-attainability-systems argument.

interlocutors.name: Sid Meier
interlocutors.work: Quoted in Rollings + Morris (2000) Game Architecture and Design, p.38
interlocutors.role: Quoted p.155 — games as 'a set of interesting choices.' Chapter's central micro-phase framing axiom. Mediated quotation — not from a Meier primary source. Sid Meier is a designer (Civilization), not a theorist. Calleja's working analog for Salen+Zimmerman 'meaningful choice.'

interlocutors.name: Andrew Rollings and Dave Morris
interlocutors.role: Source through which the Sid Meier aphorism reaches Calleja (p.155). Game-design-practice book.

interlocutors.name: Research participants (Ananke, Sunniva, Oriel, Aprile)
interlocutors.role: Four participant voices anchor key arguments. Ananke (WoW): Darkshore self-set-goal swim. Sunniva (Planetside): self-goal-control engagement. Oriel (WoW): numbers-game enthusiasm. Aprile (WoW): grinding tedium and necessity.

paradigm_worked_examples.ludic_move: GTA IV's open virtual environment supports system-validated mission-goals (linear scripted-narrative progression with strict ludic parameters) AND player-defined personal goals (drive-around-for-a-nicer-car as Schank+Abelson instrumental goal, or for-its-own-sake aesthetic goal) AND community-negotiated goals (player-arranged hospital-loop races). Across the rewards typology: spatial-area-unlock (missions gate new exploration zones), scripted-narrative (Nico cut scenes), aesthetic-beauty (harbor at sunrise). The volume's premier ludic-dimension case study.

Volume-defining ergodic-vs-non-ergodic semiosis exhibit. The flag's meaning is rule-system-assigned (locus of competitive struggle in capture-the-flag mode), not iconographic (national-patriotism in cinema). Strongest Uexküll Wirkmal (effect-marker) candidate in the volume.

Primary-goal-with-cascading-subgoals paradigm: find-fugitive-father (primary) → radio-station → equipment → town → currency → job (subgoal chain). Also alternative-primary-goal exhibit: rule-system corpse-persistence supports a murder-everyone primary goal. Demonstrates how rule-system design determines goal-set attainability.

Signature self-set-goal exhibit. Swim yields no system reward but explores the limits of traversing game-space; satisfaction derives from sense-of-agency (decide-and-do) + spatial exploration + the journey-story contributed to alterbiography. The chapter's sole occurrence of 'agency' (p.153) sits inside this discussion.

EXTENDED CASE for strategy/tactics/microtactics + ludic-economy. Primary goal: build all-Italian team and win online cup. Subgoal cascade interlocks contract-time + money + staff-hire + player-morale. Tactics: win-individual-matches; preserve-contract-time; preserve-morale. Microtactic exemplar: right-winger faced by defender — pass-to-right-back / dribble-and-cross / cross-immediately. Most elaborated single design-economy analysis in the chapter.

Performative-enhancing reward paradigm. Each level yields a skill-point; skill-points buy access to armor/weapons/vehicles; skills compound synergistically (infiltrator-suit + reconnaissance-aircraft → drop-onto-tower-rooftop-and-hack). Skill-economy is itself a ludic-economy.

Intrinsic-points reward + rhetorical amplification. 'Monster Kill' exaggerated audio-effect rhetorically AMPLIFIES the player's Purpose+Act conjunction (the strongest Burke-pentad-mapping site in the chapter — system rhetorically validates the player's motivation).

Aesthetic-beauty-as-explicit-reward paradigm (Figure 9.3 anchor). Sequence-completion bursts surroundings into color — designer explicitly couples goal-completion to aesthetic-payoff on the calmer side of the affective dimension.

three_tiers.definition: Plans formulated in pursuit of primary goals.
three_tiers.temporal_distance: Long (training regime, season-level planning, choice of which tournaments to attend).
three_tiers.fencing_example: Build a training regime + careful tournament selection toward county top-three ranking.
three_tiers.fifa09_example: Overall team-construction approach (Italian-only roster, build-cup-winning-side); shifts dynamically based on perceived possibility of attaining primary goal.

three_tiers.definition: Plans formulated in pursuit of subgoals.
three_tiers.fencing_example: Disrupt opponent's attacks while retreating; use counterattacks to score safe points.
three_tiers.fifa09_example: Match-management subgoals — win each match while avoiding injuries / send-offs; preserve player-morale via match-rotation balanced against contract-time.

three_tiers.definition: Plans formulated during the moment of action under conditions of short temporal-distance between formulation, execution, feedback, and evaluation. Identifies 'decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others.'
three_tiers.fencing_example: Opponent out of balance, foil moving clockwise — lunge with counterclockwise evasion of the blade.
three_tiers.fifa09_example: Right-winger faced by a defender at full speed — short-pass-to-right-back / dribble-and-cross / cross-immediately.

strategy_tactics_microtactics_hierarchy.temporal_distance_qualification: The strategy/tactic/microtactic distinction is useful only where there is a short temporal distance between plan-formulation, execution, feedback, and evaluation. Board games and turn-based strategy (Medieval II: Total War) do not benefit from microtactic vocabulary because players have time to think tactically. In real-time game environments where players need to act, the microtactic concept identifies decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others.
strategy_tactics_microtactics_hierarchy.dissertation_use: Portable as a coding scheme for player-deliberation analysis. Strategy / tactic / microtactic = primary-goal-plan / subgoal-plan / immediate-action-plan. The temporal-distance qualification makes the typology a graded gradient rather than a categorical taxonomy. Cleanest Aristotelian-phronesis cross-walk: strategy ↔ distal-deliberation, tactic ↔ situated-tactical-deliberation, microtactic ↔ prohairesis (deliberative choice in the moment) mediated by deliberative phantasia (imaginative-projection of action-possibilities).

rewards_typology.status: ANTICIPATORY FORMALIZATION (Calleja does not list as a typology)

categories.label: Performative-enhancing
categories.definition: Reward improves avatar/miniature abilities or grants altogether new abilities.

categories.label: Mobility-enhancing
categories.definition: Reward improves traversal efficiency / attractiveness across large worlds.

categories.label: Visibility / spatial
categories.definition: Reward grants added map-visibility for tactical decision-making (omniscient-viewpoint games).

categories.label: Spatial-area-unlock
categories.definition: Space itself functions as reward — mission-completion gates new areas for exploration.

categories.label: Intrinsic-points / score
categories.anchor: p.161 Space Invaders + Counter-Strike: Source 'Monster Kill'
categories.definition: Points / score assigned for successful action build toward a quantifiable high-score; rhetorical amplification (audio effects) optional.

categories.label: Social-acclamation (achievements)
categories.definition: Predefined-goal-unlock displayed on profile; social bragging-rights in community.

categories.label: The numbers-game (level-meters, XP, gear-stats)
categories.definition: Quantified-accumulation reward in numerical / bar-graph format; level-completion sound; grinding tolerated for level-advance lure.

categories.label: Competitive rewards
categories.anchor: p.163 CS most-kills / WoW first-guild raid
categories.definition: Numerically-quantified goal compared to competing player or group.

categories.label: Collaborative rewards (class-orientation)
categories.anchor: p.164 LOTRO Burglar / WoW Priest healing
categories.definition: Abilities that enhance one's utility in supporting others; class-choice as orientation commitment.

categories.label: Scripted-narrative-as-reward
categories.anchor: p.164 GTA IV Nico-story / MGS4 anti-paradigm p.164
categories.definition: Goal-completion triggers preset cut-scene / scripted sequence; works when graphics+voice+character carry quality, fails when non-skippable + tedious.

categories.label: Aesthetic-beauty
categories.anchor: p.165 GTA IV harbor + Flower color-burst
categories.definition: Aesthetic appreciation on calmer side of affective dimension. Flower explicitly uses aesthetic beauty as designed reward-mechanic.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.site: 'sense of agency created by allowing players to decide to do something and then to actually do it'
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.flag: Agency-as-felt — sole occurrence of 'agency' in Ch.9. No phenomenologist cite (no Husserl/Merleau-Ponty/Heidegger). Residual-phenomenology-without-phenomenologist-cite flag. Layer-A bridge candidate: Heidegger BCAP existential-analytic of decide-and-do as kairic disclosure; Aristotelian prohairesis as deliberative-choice.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.site: 'autotelic experience yielding satisfaction within a rule-based system of meaning'
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.flag: Loanword from Csikszentmihalyi WITHOUT citation. Confirms volume-wide flow-theory absence. Strongest Layer-A bridge: Aristotelian eudaimonia / praxis-for-its-own-sake (end-in-itself activity); Aristotle's NE I.7 self-sufficient-activity criterion.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.site: 'pursuing a goal can be an end in itself'
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.flag: End-in-itself praxis formulation — Aristotelian praxis-as-its-own-end signature. No Aristotle cite.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.site: 'choices that are made … in relation to the pursuit of goals'
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.flag: Choice-as-experienced is the chapter's primary phenomenological residue. No phenomenologist anchor; Calleja describes the experiential surface of choice without theorizing it phenomenologically.

residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.site: 'on-the-spot decisions … to attain the immediate goal'
residual_phenomenology_anchor_sites.flag: Microtactic-as-felt-deliberation. Internal-speech example ('He is out of balance, with the foil moving clockwise; lunge with a counterclockwise evasion of the blade') is a residual-phenomenology of moment-of-action deliberation. Cleanest Aristotelian phronesis + deliberative phantasia (Papachristou) bridge in the chapter.
Closing-summary phenomenological thesis. Repercussion-as-meaning-condition is structurally Heideggerian (sorge-as-care, world-disclosure-via-consequences) but Calleja does not invoke Heidegger here.

burke_pentad.rationale: Goals = pentadic Purpose (the 'for what / toward what end' of action). Moment-of-gameplay actions = pentadic Act (the 'what done' under Purpose's organization). Rule system = pentadic Scene (the framing context that lends Act its motive-intelligibility). The strategy/tactics/microtactics three-tier hierarchy IS a pentadic decomposition of how Purpose organizes Act at descending temporal scales (distal-Purpose / proximal-Purpose / immediate-Act). Counter-Strike 'Monster Kill' audio-amplification (p.161) is a paradigmatic Burkean motivation-rhetoric exhibit: the system RHETORICALLY AMPLIFIES the player's Purpose+Act conjunction. Calleja's repeated framing of goals as the EXPERIENTIAL manifestation of the rule system (p.149 lines 5258-5266) matches Burke's claim that pentadic Purpose is what gives Act its motive-intelligibility. THE VOLUME'S PREMIER BURKE-PENTAD-MAPPING SITE AFTER KINESTHETIC-AGENCY.

uexkull.primary_constructs: Wirkmal (effect-marker / effector-sign) + goal-structure as Funktionskreis (function-circle) + Umwelt-as-rule-mediated-action-field
uexkull.rationale: Uexküll's Funktionskreis decomposes the perception-action loop into Merkmal (perception-marker) and Wirkmal (effect-marker / effector-sign). Calleja's ludic-involvement micro-phase is paradigmatically Wirkmal-organized: actions are not raw motor-execution but rule-validated effector-signs that carry game-system meaning. The capture-the-flag flag (pp.148-149) is THE VOLUME-DEFINING WIRKMAL EXHIBIT — physical-screen-pixel-of-flag becomes effector-sign-of-ludic-objective via rule-system mediation. The goal-structure analysis maps onto Uexküll's claim that the animal's Umwelt is organized by its biological purposes (Tonkreise): the player's game-Umwelt is organized by primary-goal / subgoal / microtactic decomposition. The Sid Meier 'set of interesting choices' aphorism aligns with Uexküll's claim that the animal's Umwelt presents itself as a structured field of action-possibilities, not as a neutral perceptual flux. The Spore creature-customization case (p.156) exhibits dual-Umwelt structure: the creature has a designer-tuned biological-purpose Umwelt (function tuning) AND a player-tuned aesthetic-purpose Umwelt (mental-image tuning). Calleja has zero Uexküll vocabulary.

ontological_grounding.primary_target: Aristotelian phronesis (NE VI) + deliberative phantasia (DA III.10-11) via Papachristou + Aristotelian eudaimonia / praxis-for-its-own-sake (NE I.7) as anchor for autotelic-without-Csikszentmihalyi
ontological_grounding.rationale: Papachristou's reading of Aristotelian phronesis as embodied-deliberative-capacity-applied-to-particulars, mediated by phantasia (deliberative-imagination of action-possibilities), is the cleanest ontological grounding for Calleja's micro-phase strategy/tactics/microtactics hierarchy. The fencing case (pp.157-158) and the FIFA 09 case (pp.158-159) are paradigmatic phronesis-exhibits: agent-confronted-with-particular-situation-deliberates-among-action-possibilities-and-acts. The microtactic concept ('decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others', p.158 lines 5600-5602) is structurally identical to Aristotelian prohairesis (deliberative choice). Calleja's iterative process of planning/execution/feedback/replanning (p.156 lines 5518-5526) is a moment-by-moment exercise of practical reasoning. ADDITIONALLY: the autotelic-without-Csikszentmihalyi residual-phenomenology site (p.149 line 5280) is best bridged via Aristotelian eudaimonia / praxis-for-its-own-sake (NE I.7 self-sufficient-activity criterion + NE VI.5 distinction between praxis [end-in-itself] and poiesis [end-outside-itself]) — pursuing-a-goal-as-end-in-itself is Aristotelian praxis. Calleja has zero Aristotle hits per Phase 0 cite-check. THIS CHAPTER IS THE VOLUME'S PREMIER PHRONESIS-ANCHOR SITE.

heidegger_bcap.rationale: BCAP's analyses would deepen Calleja's planning-execution-feedback-replanning loop. Kairos is directly relevant to microtactic-as-immediate-action-choice (the right-moment to lunge with counterclockwise evasion).

bowin_amt.rationale: Bowin's analyses of continuous motion + aisthesis-kinesis interaction supply the kinematic substrate for the microtactic concept — moment-by-moment decisions that immediately translate into motor action under short temporal-distance conditions (p.158 lines 5595-5602). Strategy/tactics/microtactics descends in temporal granularity in a manner that parallels Aristotle's motion-at-different-scales analyses.

phantasia_cluster.rationale: Papachristou's deliberative-phantasia reading is the bridge between Aristotelian phronesis and the player's imaginative-projection of plan-options before execution. The Ananke Darkshore-swim self-set-goal (p.152) is a paradigmatic exhibit of phantasia-driven goal-construction. The internal-speech microtactic example ('He is out of balance ... lunge with a counterclockwise evasion') is structurally phantastic-deliberative.
